title: Add reason codes + telemetry for batching profile selection
creator: Sofia Ivanova
content:
## Context
Workload-aware batching defaults adds tier-based profiles (fast / standard / cost-efficient) with multiple override layers (request, route policy, tenant/Dedicated). During rollout and ongoing ops, we need an explainable signal for *why* the runtime selected a specific profile. This is required for:
- Console “why this profile” UX (design spec)
- SRE triage (fast-tier p99 regressions, overload behavior)
- Perf canary + regression detection (tie changes back to decision paths)

This ticket adds reason codes + structured telemetry emitted at profile-selection time.

## Goal
Expose reason codes/telemetry for why a batching profile was selected:
- tier default
- override (request/route/tenant)
- model constraint / compatibility downgrade
- overload mode behavior (e.g., tighten wait budget, shed load)

## Non-goals
- Full per-tenant auto-tuning
- High-cardinality per-request “full decision trace” in metrics (must be bounded)

## Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
### 1) Reason codes (stable, documented)
Implement a stable, versioned enum of reason codes emitted by the runtime scheduler decision point.

Must cover at minimum:
- Tier default applied
- Override applied (and which precedence tier)
- Model constraint forcing alternative profile/limits
- Overload mode behavior selection

### 2) Telemetry surfaces
Provide three surfaces:
1) **Tracing span** on the request path that includes:
   - effective tier
   - effective profile id/name
   - reason_code
   - optional reason_detail (bounded string set)
2) **Counter metric** for reason code frequency:
   - `runtime.batching.profile_selection.count`
   - labels: `tier`, `reason_code`, `model_family`, `hw_class`, `region`
3) **Sampled structured event log** (for deep dive):
   - emitted at low sampling by default; higher sampling allowed in canary
   - includes a small fixed schema for “decision inputs” (streaming flag, prompt length bucket, concurrency bucket, overload state)

### 3) Cardinality controls
- No raw route IDs or tenant IDs in metrics.
- `model_family` must be a small controlled set (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen, gemma).
- `reason_detail` must not appear in metrics labels.
- Sampling defaults must keep telemetry cost bounded.

### 4) Tests
- Unit tests for precedence mapping -> reason codes.
- Golden test for tracing field names.
- Load test sanity check: metric series growth bounded under varied traffic.

### 5) Backwards compatibility
- If reason codes are absent (older agents), behavior unchanged.
- New code must be safe under partial rollout (mixed runtime versions).

## Proposed Reason Code Set (v1)
**Core**
- `TIER_DEFAULT` — selected tier default profile
- `REQUEST_OVERRIDE` — request-level override (header/SDK param)
- `ROUTE_POLICY_OVERRIDE` — route policy explicitly set tier/profile
- `TENANT_OVERRIDE` — Dedicated/enterprise override at tenant/cluster level

**Constraints / Compatibility**
- `MODEL_CONSTRAINT_CLAMPED` — model constraints forced clamping of knobs (e.g., max_batch_tokens cap)
- `MODEL_CONSTRAINT_FALLBACK_PROFILE` — had to select a compatible profile variant for model/hw
- `QUANTIZATION_COMPAT_FALLBACK` — chosen profile compatible with active quantization variant

**Overload / Degradation**
- `OVERLOAD_TIGHTEN_WAIT_BUDGET` — tightened wait budget/admission control for tail protection
- `OVERLOAD_INCREASE_BATCHING_WITH_GUARDRAILS` — switched to more aggressive batching within guardrails
- `OVERLOAD_LOAD_SHED` — load shed / reject path taken (still emit decision telemetry)

**Legacy**
- `LEGACY_MANUAL_CONFIG` — no tiering; legacy batching knobs in effect
- `FAILSAFE_DEFAULT` — unexpected config state; used safe fallback (should page in canary)

Notes:
- We keep the enum small and stable. New codes require a version bump and docs update.
- “Override” codes must reflect precedence rules: customer override > route policy > tier default.

## Implementation Notes
- Decision point: scheduler’s profile selection function (post config resolution, pre queue admission).
- Emit a single `profile_selection` tracing span attribute set.
- Metrics emission:
  - increment counter once per request after profile decision
  - ensure it’s emitted even if request is rejected due to overload (using overload reason)
- Structured event log:
  - gated by `tiered_batching.telemetry.selection_event_sample_rate`
  - include coarse buckets only:
    - `prompt_len_bucket`: `0-128`, `129-512`, `513-2k`, `2k+`
    - `concurrency_bucket`: `0-4`, `5-16`, `17-64`, `65+`

## Links / Related Work
- GitHub: `sources/github/redwood/pr-28473-add-profile-selection-reason-codes.json` (implementation)
- Metrics labels + cardinality controls: `sources/github/redwood/pr-28492-runtime-metrics-tier-labels-and-cardinality-controls.json`
- Dedicated override precedence: `sources/github/redwood/pr-28503-dedicated-override-precedence-for-batching.json`
- Observability taxonomy draft: `sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/batching-defaults-metrics-taxonomy.json`
- Console “why this profile” design: `sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-ui-batching-recommendations.json`

## Rollout Plan
1) Land runtime changes behind flag `tiered_batching.telemetry_reason_codes` (default on in canary only).
2) Validate:
   - metric series count delta < 10% in canary
   - tracing payload size within limits
   - reason codes align with known traffic patterns (manual spot checks)
3) Enable in hosted API subset.
4) Enable by default for runtime-1.22 once SRE approves dashboards/alerts.

## Open Questions
- Do we need a separate code for “policy chose tier due to workload signals” vs “explicit tier set”? Current plan: this is implied by `TIER_DEFAULT` + a `selection_mode` field in the structured event (`explicit`/`workload_heuristic`).
- Where should `selection_mode` live? Prefer tracing + event log only (not metrics label) to avoid series explosion.

---
## Updates / Comments
### 2026-01-24 (Julian Moore)
Drafted enum list + proposed telemetry surfaces. Concern: adding `route` as a label is not viable; keeping route only in trace/event at sampling.

### 2026-02-02 (Allison Grant)
Please ensure `reason_detail` never becomes a metric label. Also add an explicit `FAILSAFE_DEFAULT` code and alert on any non-zero in canary.

### 2026-02-06 (Logan Wright)
Telemetry cost note: tracing attributes are fine; structured events must be sampled and sent via existing analytics pipeline. Provide config knob and default to 0.1% outside canary.

### 2026-02-11 (Sean Gallagher)
SRE asks that overload rejections still emit a reason code so we can correlate customer complaints with shed behavior. Also prefer paging only on fast-tier p99 regression, ticket on reason-code anomalies.

### 2026-02-19 (Julian Moore)
Implementation in progress. Added buckets for prompt length and concurrency for event logs; kept metrics clean.

### 2026-03-03 (Julian Moore)
PR up: reason code enum + trace attributes + counter metric. Added unit tests for precedence mapping (request/route/tenant). Linking PR: pr-28473.

### 2026-03-07 (Rafael Mendes)
Requested a quick canary plan: verify series growth and that `FAILSAFE_DEFAULT` stays at 0. Also confirm overload reason codes appear during synthetic overload test.

### 2026-03-12 (Julian Moore)
Addressed review feedback:
- Removed any temptation to include `profile_id` as a metric label (kept in trace/event only)
- Added `model_family` normalization table
- Added guardrail: unknown reason code maps to `FAILSAFE_DEFAULT` + increments `runtime.batching.profile_selection.failsafe.count`

### 2026-03-18 (Sofia Ivanova)
Approved. Please coordinate with ENG-18429 so dashboards pick up the new metric and reason_code breakdown.

### 2026-03-24 (Julian Moore)
Merged + enabled in canary by default. Initial canary check: metric series +6% (within budget), `FAILSAFE_DEFAULT` = 0, overload tests show `OVERLOAD_LOAD_SHED` as expected. Marking Done.
